» What is the GIL? » A mutex (mutual exclusion lock) that protects access to Python objects in CPython (the default Python implementation). » Ensures that only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time. » Why does it exist? » Simplifies memory management in CPython, especially with reference counting for garbage collection. » Avoids race conditions and ensures thread safety in single-threaded contexts. » Implications for Multithreading » Limits true parallelism in CPU-bound tasks, as only one thread can execute Python code at any moment. » I/O-bound tasks can still benefit from multithreading since the GIL is released during I/O operations (e.g., file I/O, network requests).

» Evented systems react to the facts communicated to them.
» Logs are hard to process in batch systems due to the speed and size of data.
Companies push log data as events into a data stream to perform stream processing.
» Modern web applications track user actions such as clicks and page views. » These actions add up fast, overwhelming traditional data stores.
» Stream processing allows companies to process data as it's generated and not hours after the fact as is common with batch processing.
» Real Time Pricing adjusts to environmental factors and instantaneous demand.

» Scheduled analysis of related groups of data » As up to date as the last scheduled run » May run for long periods of time » Often involve mutable data stores » May access all historical data.

» Real-time analysis of data as it is produced » Runs as soon as event is produced » As up to date as the last event generated » Often involves immutable data stores » Often uses recently produced, windowed data » May not give us a full historical picture.

» The differences are generalizations, not hard rules. » Most data engineering teams use both batch and stream processing together to achieve their goals. » Stream processing complements batch processing.
» Stream Processing applications consist of a streaming data store and the streaming calculation(s).
» Streaming data stores hold all of the immutable event data in a system. » These data stores guarantee that data is stored in the order it was produced.

» Apache Kafka and Apache Cassandra are examples of streaming data stores. » Apache Kafka is the highway system + traffic logbook for events in motion. » Apache Cassandra is the massive, distributed parking lot + address system for fast, always-on storage.
» Popular Stream Processing tools, all of which share common features, include Confluent KSQL, Kafka Streams, Faust, Spark Structured Streaming, Apache Flink, and Samza.
This decouples applications from each other » Immutable data provides pipeline repeatability.
» Faster calculations on windowed data (real-time) » More scalable due to distributed nature of data stores » Decouples how data is used from how it is produced.
